limitations: The two genes absent from the GTEx file (1,485 − 1,483 = 2) are excluded from all per-tissue statistics; their identity and reason for absence (e.g., not assayed in GTEx) are not recorded in the source files.

Spearman correlation and median |log2 ratio| are computed on raw nTPM values without batch correction or normalization beyond the nTPM scaling already applied by each source; residual platform effects (different RNA-seq protocols, library preparation, alignment pipelines) may contribute to the observed discrepancies.
The top-20 and top-10 lists are sensitive to the exact nTPM values at the boundary; a small change in a gene's nTPM near rank 20 or 10 could alter list membership.
RNA tissue specificity categories are assigned by HPA based on its own expression data and may not reflect GTEx-based specificity; they are reported as context, not as an independent validation.

The consensus nTPM values shown in the top-10 discrepancy tables confirm that the consensus tracks the higher (GTEx) value in most cases, consistent with a geometric-mean aggregation, but the exact aggregation formula used by HPA for the consensus file is not documented in the source data.

limitations: The consensus nTPM is a deterministic function of the HPA and GTEx values; it cannot serve as an independent replication and its agreement with either source is circular by construction.
The gene universe is restricted to the 1,485 TF Ensembl genes present in the HPA master table; TFs absent from HPA are excluded from all analyses.
Spearman correlation measures rank agreement only; the median |log2 ratio| captures typical magnitude of absolute discrepancy but does not characterise the full distribution.
Two of the 1,485 TF genes had no GTEx row in at least one tissue and were excluded from eligibility, reducing the eligible set to 1,483 per tissue.
